Ingredients
20 oz ground turkey
16 oz butternut squash
4 scallions
2 cans black beans
2 tomato paste
1 Tex-Mex paste (all)
2 tbsp Southwest spice blend
2 limes
8 tbsp yogurt
1/2 cup white cheddar
Pantry: oil, salt, pepper

1. Wash produce. Chop squash into bite-size pieces. Slice scallions, keeping whites and greens apart. Quarter the lime.
2. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium-high. Add turkey and Southwest spice. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Cook turkey, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes.
4. Add squash and scallion whites. Stir now and then until scallions soften, 2-4 minutes.
5. Stir in all the tomato paste and all the Tex-Mex paste. Cook until slightly darker, 1-2 minutes.
6. Add the beans with their liquid, 2 cups water, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
7. Simmer, stirring now and then, until chili thickens and squash is tender, 12-15 minutes. Turn off heat.
8. Too thick? Add a splash of water. Season with a squeeze of lime, salt and pepper.
9. Serve in bowls topped with yogurt, scallion greens and the cheddar. Lime wedges on the side.

Ingredients
1 lb sirloin steak, cubed
4 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp butter
1 cup green beans

1. Pat the steak dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
2. Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the steak and cook for 5 minutes, turning once, until browned.
3. Add the green beans and cook for 4 minutes until bright green and tender.
4. Lower the heat, add the butter and garlic, and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
5. Plate the steak and beans, spoon over the garlic butter, and enjoy!
